correctness.rationale: Because distinct vertices incoming directed-arc collections are disjoint, each in-degree histogram is multinomial with binomial cell probabilities; likewise for outgoing. An in-degree at i and out-degree at j share exactly one Bernoulli arc j->i if i!=j (none when i=j). Law of total covariance yields mixed entries n(n-1)p(1-p)(h_{k-1}-h_k)(h_{l-1}-h_l). Binomial score identity converts to rank-one n v v^T after whitening. u=sqrt(b) and v=standardized binomial score are orthonormal; in the 2n space, (u,0),(0,u),(v,-v) are three zeros; (v,v) has 2n; orthocomplement has n with multiplicity 2n-4. The whitened in-minus-out difference has covariance 2n(Id-uu^T-vv^T), so the mean Pearson contrast is n-2 exactly. Independently enumerated every directed loopless graph for n=2,3 at p=1/3,2/3 using exact rational probabilities, matching each covariance entry; the all-n proof uses the one-shared-arc lemma, not enumeration.
residual_risks: Requires opposite directed arcs independent, no loops, n>=2 and 0<p<1.
Exact finite Pearson expectation is not a chi-square distribution or asymptotic normality claim.
